Pool Service in Glendale, AZ, Where the Tap Water Comes From Three Places

Glendale blends river water, Colorado River water and well water, and the mix shows up on pool tile and equipment. Call the free line any hour to be put through to an independent, locally owned pool service company that works in Glendale.

Pool service in Glendale, AZ starts with the water coming out of your hose. The city draws on the Salt and Verde rivers, the Colorado River and its own wells, and a pool that is topped off week after week keeps every mineral that water carries. This page covers what that means for a Glendale pool, what drives the price of service, and how to get connected with a pool company near you at no cost.

Phoenix Pool Cleaning Pro does not clean or repair pools. Glendale: one city, three sources of tap water

The City of Glendale lists three sources for its drinking water. Salt River Project water is snowmelt and rain runoff from the Salt and Verde river watersheds. Central Arizona Project water is runoff from the Colorado River watershed, carried across the desert by canal. Groundwater is pumped from city wells. The city also uses reclaimed water, but only for things like landscape irrigation, not for drinking or filling pools.

Those supplies reach homes through more than one treatment plant. Arizona's state drinking water database lists Pyramid Peak, Cholla and Oasis among the active sources for Glendale's system. Pyramid Peak sits in north Phoenix and is shared with Peoria: Glendale owns 77 percent of it and runs it, and it serves the northern parts of both cities. In a June 2025 water resources update, the city put its yearly CAP supply at 22,582 acre-feet, delivered by canal to Pyramid Peak and usable anywhere in the city's service area.

Services Glendale pool owners ask about

Most calls are for steady weekly care: skimming, brushing, emptying baskets, testing and balancing the water. The pool cleaning and weekly maintenance page explains what a visit should include. Hard fill water makes pool tile cleaning a common request, because scale tends to show first as a white or gray line where the water meets the tile. When a pump hums, a filter leaks or a heater will not fire, pool repair takes over. If you are not sure which of these you need, start with the overview of pool service in Phoenix.

What Glendale's hardness numbers mean for a pool

A 2023 water quality report put City of Glendale water at 153 to 309 parts per million of hardness, roughly 9 to 18 grains per gallon. The report notes that hardness is not a health standard. For a pool, though, the spread matters.

The top-off water varies

With several sources and plants in the system, the hardness of the water at your hose can be near the low end of that range or near the top. Two Glendale pools a few miles apart can drift at different speeds.

Evaporation leaves minerals behind

Water leaves the pool as vapor, but calcium does not. Each top-off adds more, so calcium hardness (the amount of dissolved calcium in the water) creeps up over the months, even when the water looks clear.

Scale shows up in two places

You can see it on tile and the waterline. You cannot see it inside a heater or on salt cell plates, where it cuts efficiency. Ask the pool company to test calcium hardness, not just chlorine and pH.

Pool service in Glendale, AZ: what sets the price

Price is usually the first question, and the honest answer is that each company sets its own. The line does not quote or set prices. What it can do is tell you what moves a quote up or down, so you can compare two companies fairly.

  • Pool size and shapeA larger pool or one with steps, benches and a spa takes longer to brush and vacuum.
  • What each visit includesSome plans cover skimming, brushing, baskets and water testing only. Others add filter cleaning on a schedule. Ask for the list.
  • ChemicalsAsk whether chemicals are part of the monthly number or billed by use. Pools with high calcium or high stabilizer can need more attention.
  • Trees and debrisCitrus, palms and desert trees near the water mean fuller baskets and more time at each stop.
  • EquipmentSalt systems, heaters and automation add things to check. Repairs are always quoted on their own.

For published cost ranges with their sources, read the pool service cost guide. Real quotes in Glendale will vary with the pool in front of the technician.

Safe checks before you call

  • Baskets. Empty the skimmer basket and, with the pump off, the pump basket. A packed basket starves the pump.
  • Water level. The water should reach about the middle of the skimmer opening. Too low and the pump can suck air.
  • Filter gauge. Note the pressure reading and tell the company. A reading well above normal points to a dirty filter.
  • Timer. Check that the pump schedule did not reset after a power blip.
  • Breaker. Reset a tripped pool breaker or GFCI once. If it trips again, leave it off and call.

Chemicals and children. Never mix pool chemicals with each other. Store them apart, dry and shaded, and out of children's reach, and follow the label. Keep children away from a pool that is not fenced or covered, and treat green or cloudy water as a drowning hazard, because no one can see the bottom.

Check the license first. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) licenses contractors, and its residential classifications include R-6, Swimming Pool Service and Repair. Routine cleaning and water care are generally not treated as contracting work, but repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a licensed contractor. Ask the company for its ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search (opens in a new tab) before work begins. The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Who handles pool service in Glendale, AZ?

Call the free line, any hour. A recorded assistant takes down the pool problem and your part of Glendale, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned pool service company. That company quotes, does the work and bills you. The line itself never charges you.

How much does pool service cost in Glendale, AZ?

There is no single Glendale price. Weekly service is usually quoted by the month, and the number moves with the size of the pool, whether there is a spa, the equipment, how much debris lands in the water and whether chemicals are part of the plan or billed on top. Repairs are quoted separately. Ask for the quote in writing and ask exactly what each visit covers. The pool service cost guide explains the published ranges and what moves them.

Do you take calls from the 85308 ZIP code?

Yes. The line takes calls from 85308 and every other ZIP code in and around Glendale. Tell the assistant your cross streets or neighborhood so the call goes to a company that works near you.

Is Glendale tap water hard enough to scale a pool?

It can be. A 2023 water quality report put the hardness of City of Glendale water at 153 to 309 parts per million, about 9 to 18 grains per gallon. Pools lose water to evaporation and get topped off, so the minerals in the fill water build up in the pool over time and can leave white scale on tile and inside equipment. Hard water is not a health concern, but it is a maintenance one.

Does a Glendale pool company need a license?

Routine cleaning and water care are generally not treated as contracting work in Arizona. Repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a contractor licensed by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Ask for the ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search before work starts.
